items.content:
Earlier gameplay summary (agent-written, uncertain claims remain uncertain):
Game/context: Untitled Goose Game, single-player Save 01; no task list or explicit objectives appeared. The stump’s pickup tutorial was seen. Known route: wooded clearing -> northeast around rocks/bushes -> stream/stepping stones -> fallen log/far bank -> large rock and brown boot -> red bicycle junction -> stump with blue-and-white can -> looping dirt path -> signpost/gate. Gate area has green cup, gate posts, rails, diagonal plank, hedge and rock wall; stump area also has a small brown cup-like object on open ground.

Controls/mechanics observed: Left-click walks to a destination; holding/dragging left steers and is often more reliable than short clicks. Tutorial listed double-click/Shift run, Z/right-click grab, Space honk, Ctrl/C crouch/bend, X flap, A/S zoom. Ctrl bends the neck in body-facing direction, not automatically toward the pointer. Clear-ground waypoints work; clicks near roots, hedge, signpost or gate often stall or merely turn. Camera pans displace pointer aim. Tab opens delayed Controls notebook, Escape closes after delay; overlays may swallow input. Crossing the log required sustained Ctrl+left steering through water/under it; clicking beyond alone failed. Boot was briefly lifted with close Ctrl+right mouse but not carried. Stepping-stone usability unconfirmed.

Pickup history: No pickup/carry has ever been confirmed. At the green cup, many east/west/north/south approaches overshot, left it behind the beak or beneath the body, or pushed the goose into hedge/gate geometry. Numerous stationary Ctrl+right-click holds, separate bend-then-click attempts, re-aimed attempts and Ctrl+Z failed. Once the cup showed white interaction marks while directly targeted, but still did not lift. Whenever hidden, subsequent movement showed it remained on the ground. Never assume an obscured object is held; it must visibly stay at the beak and travel with the goose. Working input hypothesis: pre-aim in a separate pointer action because pointer movement during a combined control action may occur after the button press; this timing was not directly verified.

Gate observations: Diagonal plank and posts obstruct approaches. Close Ctrl+right-click and separate right-click attempts at the exposed plank left it visibly fixed; no passage opened. Moving the plank remains only a speculative interaction. Gate is visibly barred by rails and diagonal plank.

Recent navigation: After repeated green-cup failures, the goose moved back to the stump. Direct clicks stalled against its upper/right side; steering east around it reached clear grass. The brown cup-like object was then approached from northeast. Latest confirmed observation: goose on clear grass northeast of the brown object, facing southwest, object visible ahead beside stump but still outside beak range. A final completed left-click at normalized (0.515,0.805), intended to stop just northeast of it, has not been observed. Green cup was left near gate/hedge; blue can remains by stump.

Active goals/hypotheses: First verify the final click’s result and relocate the brown object. If correctly positioned, pre-aim at it, hold Ctrl and right-click without pointer movement, then move to confirm carry. The unobstructed brown object may be easier than the green cup, but this is only a hypothesis. If alignment is poor, create open-ground separation and make a straight approach with object ahead at lowered-neck range; avoid close turns or grabbing when it is behind/beneath the body. After resolving pickup tutorial, inspect gate for a passage/interaction.
